doc.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025

chapter: Famous sessions and the guitar sound
title: Charlie Calello walks out on Richie Havens
summary: The worst session he remembers: Charlie Calello producing Richie Havens stormed out over the drummer and never finished the record.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Have you ever had a right time/wrong – what’s the worst session you ever did? The worst gig?
The worst gig I ever did? MR; The worst gig ever, anything come to mind like oh man that was just –
Well I remember a gig that was a little painful as far as – at the Record Plant we were going to do I’m trying to think of his name who sang “Freedom” at Woodstock.
Jesus I can’t think of his name. Losing my brain. Richie Havens.

Richie Havens yeah. And it was Charlie Calello was producing Richie Havens. And Charlie was a great arranger. He did all the Four Seasons arrangements and stuff like that and you know he’s the one the came up with [scats]. Great arranger. But he was producing Richie Havens. And somebody was playing drums and he was not happy with the drums, he kept changing the drum part and the drummer couldn’t remember like what he wanted. And he’d start the take and we’d get to the part and he wouldn’t play what Charlie wanted. And Charlie was a great arranger, really a great pop arranger. But for some reason something was happening, he wasn’t happy with the drummer. And Richie was getting nervous. Richie was used to playing with folk singers and playing with guys, then all of a sudden there’s a – he’s being produced by Charlie Calello. And Charlie got upset with the drummer and threw his pencil down and walked out of the studio and got in the cab and left, and just left us all in the studio like – and Richie was like – I didn’t know what to say to Richie. The drummer was embarrassed. And that was a strange session. And I walked out of there just feeling like wow. We were all trying to do the right thing but Charlie wasn’t happy and he just slammed his pencil down on the podium and walked out and got a cab and went home. Never finished the record. That was a weird moment in the studio.
Yeah. Well no one got hurt except their feelings.
No. There was no blood. It wasn’t Viet Nam. It’s okay.
